faq.a: Hadiza is associated with the Arabic form خَدِيجَة, whose core sense is hadiza; khadija (hausa form).

faq.q: What is the origin of Hadiza?
faq.a: Hadiza is associated with Arabic. Hadiza is the Hausa form of Arabic خَدِيجَة (Khadīja), the name of the Prophet's first wife.
Yes — the underlying form خَدِيجَة is Arabic.
Hadiza can occur in Muslim naming contexts, but it is better described as a Arabic-origin name used within some Muslim naming traditions than as an exclusively Islamic religious term.
Hadiza should not be classified as a Quranic personal name without a direct Quranic basis. Khadīja is not a Quranic personal name.

faq.q: What does Hadiza mean in Urdu?
faq.a: In Urdu, Hadiza is rendered خدیجہ and carries the sense خدیجہ، زوجہ نبی.

faq.q: What does Hadiza mean in Persian?
faq.a: In Persian, Hadiza is rendered خدیجه and carries the sense خدیجه، نام همسر پیامبر.
A romanized syllable approximation is ha-di-za. No IPA transcription is asserted because a verified phonetic transcription was not available.

faq.q: What are the variants of Hadiza?
faq.a: Romanization variants include Hadiza, hadiza. Script forms are خديجه, خدیجه, خدیجہ, خَدِيجَة, हदीज़ा.

faq.q: Is Hadiza a boy's or girl's name?
faq.a: Documented usage records this form as female. Gender is not inferred from the meaning of the word, and actual use may vary between communities.
